newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: German refiners resist run cuts despite poor margins.
newsitem.headline: German refiners resist run cuts despite poor margins.

text.p: Refineries in Germany so far have resisted the pressure to cut back on output even though sagging margins in Northwest Europe have forced oil firms in the ARA region to trim production, the companies and traders said on Thursday.
German major Veba said it had not reduced output at its 210,000 barrel per day Gelsenkirchen plant.
"There have been no cutbacks," a spokeswoman said.
RWE-DEA said it too had not engaged in run cuts. The company has the 80,000 bpd Heide and 120,000 bpd Wesseling refineries as well as a stake in the 280,000 bpd Miro refinery in Karlsruhe.
"It's right we have had very poor margins, but it hasn't been sufficient reason for us to cut runs," a company source said.
An Esso spokesman said there had been no changes at its 105,000 bpd Ingolstadt refinery.
Deutsche Shell declined to comment, but German traders said its Godorf and Harburg refineries appeared to be operating at or near full capacity.
In the ARA region, the picture has been quite different.
On Thursday, Texaco Inc said it had increased crude cut runs to 12.5 percent at the two Nerefco refineries it shares with with British Petroleum.
Trade sources said Shell crude throughput at its 374,00 bpd Rotterdam refinery had fallen by 12-15 percent, a cut equivalent to 50,000 bpd.
At the start of the week, Universal, owned by Daewoo Corp, cut runs at its 60,000 bpd Antwerp refinery by 15 percent.
Traders in the ARA region said that other refineries had followed suit.
A BP spokesman said the company did not comment on run cuts, but suggested they may be likely.
"In the light of very poor margins, BP is constantly reviewing throughput at its refineries and is fine-tuning accordingly," he said.
An Esso spokesman declined to comment on runs at the company's Rotterdam refinery 180,00 bpd refinery.
Total said its Flushing refinery was operating as before.
